findings.description: The recorded session-1 close strategy is unbuildable: it says to leave non-bookkeeping files uncommitted for session 2, but the close gate refuses any such dirty files.
findings.failureScenario: The operator follows D3, commits only `docs/session-framework-spec.md` and `docs/session-framework-plan.md`, leaves `docs/session-framework-build-instructions.md` and `docs/session-sets/148-the-session-framework/spec.md` for session 2, then runs `ai_router.session close`; the `working_tree_clean` gate rejects those files, so session 1 cannot close. This is probable because D3 explicitly instructs that state.

findings.description: The design keeps direct API verification as a supported path but misses that OpenAI direct API calls cannot authenticate.
findings.failureScenario: A no-seat/API-transport user runs session verification with an Anthropic or Google author; the configured `session-verification` override selects an OpenAI model, but `_call_openai` sends `Authorization: ******`, so every real OpenAI request fails authentication. This is probable for the supported “anyone without a seat” path because OpenAI is an enabled configured verifier.
